messages:
support-alex: heads up — customer ACME on Dedicated pool prod-dc-7 reports sudden throughput drop starting ~2026-03-16T12:08Z. seeing 429s + occasional 503s, overall token/sec down ~55%. ticket #INC-4542. filing here for runtime triage

maria-eng: thx alex, can you paste a sample error payload or logs? also which model and route are they pinned to?

support-alex: route: /v1/generate (redwood-hosted endpoint -> dedicated pool). model: gptx-16q (quantized), max_tokens=2048, typical requests per call ~avg 120 tokens. sample error: `{"error":{"code":429,"message":"request rate exceeded"}}`

sam-runtime: curious — did autoscaler do anything around that time? show me scaling events.

ops-bot: autoscale event: pool prod-dc-7 scaled DOWN from 8 -> 6 at 2026-03-16T12:05:12Z (policy: idle-rebalance), scaled UP from 6 -> 7 at 12:22:03Z (policy: cpu).

jinx-oncall: timeline looks like capacity dip preceeds complaints. But 429s indicate throttling at scheduler/batcher level, not strictly node loss. Could be packing inefficiency or a microburst of large prompts starving continuous batch windows.

maria-eng: I pulled runtime logs for pool prod-dc-7 around 12:00-12:30. Observations: continuous-batcher drain latency increased, avg pack efficiency dropped from 0.88 -> 0.52, and prefill queue growth spikes when large requests arrive. Also a spike in KV cache misses for prompt prefixes.

sam-runtime: packing efficiency 0.52 is huge. any recent config change? max_batch_tokens? quantum?

kevin-ml: we shipped a default tweak last week that raised default max_batch_tokens to 4096 for gptx-16q to improve throughput on long-context workloads. Might be backfiring with mixed short/long workload.

maria-eng: bingo. logs show many small requests (20-60 tokens) waiting behind a few oversized prepends (2000+ tokens). continuous-batcher waits to reach token budget and ends up creating very thin microbatches while large ones block KV slot usage. That increases per-request latency and reduces aggregate throughput.

jinx-oncall: repro steps from customer (shortened):
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gptx-16q","prompt":"<user chat>","max_tokens":2048}'
```
If you flood with interleaved short and long prompts you can reproduce queue growth in ~60s.

sam-runtime: quick mitigation: rolling revert default max_batch_tokens -> 2048 for gptx-16q on Dedicated pools (hotfix) and enable opportunistic packing threshold (pack short requests earlier if head-of-queue has been waiting >150ms). I'll push a config canary to prod-dc-7.

maria-eng: also lowering prefill_timeout from 80ms -> 50ms on that pool for now. That reduces waiting for big tokens but might slightly increase compute inefficiency.

ops-bot: deploy started: runtime-config/prod-dc-7 canary (max_batch_tokens=2048, prefill_timeout=50ms, opportunistic_pack=true) at 2026-03-16T12:58:10Z

support-alex: customer confirmed partial recovery at 12:59 UTC, errors reduced but latency still ~30% above baseline. they're asking about root cause and whether billing was impacted (they saw a few failed requests billed).

kevin-ml: billing note — failed requests that returned 429 were not billed; 503 responses sometimes resulted from partial token emit and were billed for emitted tokens. ops, can we follow up with finance?

jinx-oncall: created follow-up ticket BILL-789 for finance to audit charges for INC-4542. Also capturing SDK telemetry to flag retries that could have duplicated charges.

sam-runtime: post-canary metrics: pack efficiency recovered to 0.81 within 7 min; throughput up ~42% vs trough. prefill queue length back to normal. We'll keep the canary for three more pools and schedule a config rollback to stable defaults if no regressions.

maria-eng: next steps: 1) run a replay test on staging with mixed short/long interleaved workload to validate opportunistic_pack behavior; 2) add alert on pack_efficiency < 0.6 in Dedicated pools; 3) add a proactive autoscaler-safety check to avoid aggressive downscale while pack_efficiency < 0.7.

support-alex: customer happy with mitigation but wants commitment on permanent fix — will update ticket with runbook and ETA. thanks all. :thumbsup:
